subject: Discovery: p95 & streaming UX targets — mutual action plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moore <alex.moore@finlytics.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery: p95 & streaming UX targets — mutual action plan

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from my side and the suggested next steps so we stay aligned. Please let me know if I misremember anything.

Key pain points you described
- Burstiness during market opens leads to sharp p95 spikes (observed > 1.5s for short prompts).
- First-token latency for streaming is felt by traders — goal is a snappier streaming UX (first token visible within ~150–250ms).
- Existing system (self-hosted TF-based model pool) handles throughput but has high tail latency under concurrent KV-cache misses.

Current stack notes (as discussed)
- Model: Llama-2-13B quantized on Triton-like serving layer (custom wrappers).
- Frontend: React streaming UI that expects incremental tokens via websocket.
- Autoscaling: horizontal with conservative cooldowns; often slow to spin up on burst.

Success criteria (what Finlytics would call a win)
- p95 end-to-end generation latency for 32-token responses <= 450ms at steady-state traffic patterns.
- First-token delivered to client UI <= 250ms for streaming flows 90% of the time.
- Concurrent sustained throughput target: 800–1,200 qps (with burst headroom to 2k).
- No change to data residency requirements (must run in-us, VPC peering preferred).

Immediate technical hypotheses (what we want to validate in the PoC)
1) Prefix/KV caching for frequent prompts will reduce p95 by ~30–50% for repeat flows.
2) Model variant (int8/4 quantization and kernel tuning) + batching windows can hit p95 targets without sacrificing cost excessively.
3) Smart routing (cold-warm pools) will keep tail latency stable during bursts.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan)
- Redwood: share a short MOP checklist and a sample latency-trace collection guide (I attached a checklist + example traces). Target: by Mon 11/23.
- Finlytics: share 3 representative trace samples (burst + normal + warm cache) and a short note on your current autoscaling policy. Target: Tue 11/24.
- Schedule a 45-minute technical deep-dive (engineers only) to go over traces and confirm tuning knobs. Proposed slots: Wed 11/25 10:00–10:45 PT or Thu 11/26 09:00–09:45 PT.
- After traces review, Redwood will propose a scoped PoC (1–2 week perf-focused run) with clear MOP and metrics for pass/fail.

Attachments: redwood-mop-checklist.pdf (MOP outline), latency-traces-samples.zip (example traces).

If that aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive. Thanks again — I think there’s a clear path to hit the p95 + streaming-UX goals with a focused PoC.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Moore <alex.moore@finlytics.io>

Subject: Re: Discovery: p95 & streaming UX targets — mutual action plan

Thanks Soojin — this is a very accurate summary. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The worst-case p95 we measured was around ~1.6s during the 8:30am market open spike (mix of cache misses + cold containers).
- For streaming, the UI considers anything >300ms for first token to be degraded; our internal target is <200ms but we can accept up to 250ms in a PoC.
- Autoscaling: we have an AWS autoscaling group with a 5-minute scale-up min; we can provide the CloudWatch alarms and scaling policy.

Procurement note: looping in Procurement in case PoC requires contractual/hosted trial fees. Procurement contact: procurement@finlytics.io (they prefer short SOW + standard DPA for hosted evaluation).

We can do Wed 11/25 10:00–10:45 PT for the technical deep-dive — Karthik, can you lead the tuning/warm-pool discussion?

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the MOP checklist. I’ll ask the infra team to pull the three traces and send them by 11/24.

— Alex
Alex Moore

alex.moore@finlytics.io

Thanks everyone — calendar invite sent for Wed 11/25 10:00–10:45 PT. Attaching the checklist and sample traces now for Alex’s infra team to review.

Quick logistical notes before the deep-dive:
- Please include someone familiar with your autoscaling policies and CloudWatch alarms; we’ll want exact thresholds to model expected spin-up times.
- If you can anonymize traces, that’s fine; we only need timing and request distribution.
- If Finlytics is open to a short hosted trial, Marissa will follow up with proposed credit amount and SOW language after the technical review.

Attachments: redwood-mop-checklist.pdf (MOP + PoC pass/fail metrics), latency-traces-samples.zip (3 traces: open-spike.json, steady-state.json, warm-cache.json)

On Wed we’ll aim to come away with: 1) a clear pass/fail definition for p95 & first-token, 2) a concrete list of infra changes/data we need to run the PoC, and 3) a high-level timeline for the PoC.
